_comment: Gate 4N-I4. Provenance for the extracted hashicorp/aws provider binary, per platform. `binaries` records a SHA-256 for platforms where we have independently verified the extracted file; this is the strongest assurance and protects a long-lived local cache against POST-init tampering, which the lockfile cannot detect (its zh:/h1: entries hash the release ZIP). `lockfile_verified_platforms` lists platforms where the only assurance is the verification `tofu init` itself performs against .terraform.lock.hcl — appropriate for ephemeral CI runners that download fresh each run. Listing a platform there is a deliberate, reviewable reduction in assurance, not a silent fallback: an UNLISTED platform is FORBIDDEN.
_lockfile_verified_rationale: GitHub-hosted runners are ephemeral and fetch the provider fresh each run; `tofu init` fails closed if the download does not match the lockfile hashes, so the release artifact is authenticated. What that does NOT cover is tampering with an already-extracted binary between init and use, which cannot occur meaningfully inside a single ephemeral job. Record a binary SHA-256 here instead if the runner ever becomes self-hosted or caches .terraform across jobs.
